references.text: Gideon distributed torches, jars, and horns to the three hundred men and gave them instructions to shout, 'For the Lord and for Gideon!' - this is the immediate context for verse 20.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon, and he blew the trumpet - this shows the earlier use of the shofar in Gideon's calling.
Instructions to blow trumpets in war as a sign that the Lord will remember His people and save them from their enemies.
At the conquest of Jericho, horns and shouts were also used as war cries, similar to Gideon's tactics.
David declares that the battle belongs to the Lord - the same theological theme as 'Sword for the Lord and for Gideon'.
King Jehoshaphat and Judah achieved victory by praising the Lord, not through conventional warfare - a pattern similar to Gideon's victory.
Paul describes how we have this treasure in jars of clay - possibly an allusion to Gideon's jars that hid the light.
